condition: Post-operative urinary retention after inguinal hernia repair
summary: 71-year-old man with untreated LUTS, 8 h after open inguinal mesh repair under GA with morphine and 1.5 L IV fluid: unable to void, suprapubic discomfort, bladder scan 920 mL.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Unable to pass urine after hernia operation
inputs.hpi: Day-case open right inguinal mesh repair under general anaesthetic this morning; 1.5 L IV fluid and morphine in recovery. Has not passed urine for 8 hours despite trying; lower abdominal discomfort and urge. Before surgery: poor stream and nocturia twice nightly, never treated.

exam.general: Uncomfortable. HR 84, BP 148/86, RR 16, SpO2 97% on air, T 36.8°C.
exam.abdomen: Palpable, dull, tender bladder to 3 cm below the umbilicus. Groin wound dry, no haematoma.

surgicalHistory: Open right inguinal mesh hernia repair (today)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Post-operative urinary retention — after open inguinal hernia repair
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute post-operative urinary retention (bladder 920 mL) after hernia repair, opioids and IV fluid, background LUTS. Urethral catheter, record residual, alpha-blocker and trial without catheter.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Triage emergency_now (score 45 = age + pain + 'Post-operative or recent-procedure concern' 25): uncomfortable but stable retention.
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Post-operative ward reviews: score post-op concern from physiology (NEWS2) rather than adding 'Post-operative concern' (urgent) for any 'post-op'/'wound' word; reserve emergency_now for physiological or peritonitic criteria.

mustExclude.note: PSA is falsely raised by retention and catheterisation; defer it.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: The urinary_retention protocol lists 'U&E, eGFR, PSA (once catheterised)' as an urgent investigation (it also says 'PSA reassay at 6 weeks'), and the preventative prompt adds PSA. PSA is falsely raised by retention and catheterisation.
mustExclude.proposedFix: Remove PSA from the acute retention investigations; keep 'PSA at ≥6 weeks if indicated' in follow-up.

guideline.name: Postoperative urinary retention — anaesthetic and perioperative considerations (review)
guideline.section: Bladder ultrasound; catheterise when bladder volume exceeds 600 mL and the patient cannot void; risk factors include age, male sex, hernia surgery, anaesthetic agents, opioids and IV fluid volume
guideline.citation: Baldini G, Bagry H, Aprikian A, Carli F. Anesthesiology. 2009;110:1139–57.

guideline.name: EAU guidelines — management of non-neurogenic male LUTS (acute urinary retention)
guideline.section: Catheterise; alpha-blocker before a trial without catheter improves success
guideline.citation: Gravas S, Gacci M, Gratzke C, et al. EAU Guidelines on the management of non-neurogenic male LUTS. Arnhem: EAU; 2023.

guideline.name: PHE Prostate Cancer Risk Management Programme — PSA testing
guideline.section: Defer PSA testing after urinary retention, catheterisation or active UTI (falsely raised)
guideline.citation: Public Health England. Prostate cancer risk management programme: benefits and risks of PSA testing. London: PHE; 2016.

rationale: Base post-operative urinary retention: common after hernia surgery in older men with LUTS. Tests diagnosis, catheterisation, alpha-blocker/TWOC and PSA timing.
